svg.title: Narly fortune controller wiring schematic (as built 2026-09-23)
svg.desc: Arduino Uno on USB power; S-100-5 5V 20A supply feeding the breadboard top rail and a WS2812B strip through the rail; 12V wall adapter feeding an HX-916 coin acceptor through a barrel-jack adapter; all grounds common on the breadboard top negative rail. D2 reads the coin signal through 110 ohms; D6 drives LED data through 330 ohms. Arduino 5V pin unconnected.
svg.text: As built 2026-09-23 · PIR sensor and toggle switches (Phase 4) not yet wired · pins match fortune-controller.ino
Screw terminals, left → right under cover
Breadboard top power rail (between Arduino and terminal strip) · bottom rail unused
D6 = LED_PIN: WS2812B data, GRB, NUM_LEDS 180
3 m · 60 LED/m · 180 px · JST 3-pin in use
1. All three supplies (PSU1, PS2, laptop USB) share one ground on the breadboard top − rail. Without it D2 and D6 have no reference.
2. The Uno's 5V pin is deliberately unconnected. The Uno runs from USB; PSU1 powers only the strip.
3. Strip current returns through the breadboard rail and jumpers (≈1–2 A safe). Keep animations dim and don't raise the brightness cap.
4. Recommended rework (strip fed from PSU1 T4 / T7, C1 moved to strip end) is described in README, not shown here.
